<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Enable best-effort NUMA binding by default for eligible GPU multiprocessing launches, using soft memory preference. Explicit binding keeps its existing strict memory policy.

This continues [ivanium/vllm#53](https://github.com/ivanium/vllm/pull/53) by Yifan Qiao (@ivanium). His original commit `788505bea2c6cae925fce4afe47195188656896d` was cherry-picked with authorship, co-author trailers, and sign-offs preserved. The branch is rebased onto main (`775fefa804ca`), including the merged shared GPU-indexing fix [#61237](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61237).

## Claims

- Validate fresh host-local GPU-to-NUMA topology in the launcher, then pass the decision and mapping to children. Preserve constrained CPU affinity and existing non-default memory policies in automatic mode.
- Automatically prefer GPU-local memory with `--preferred`; EngineCore uses `--preferred-many` for multi-node shards. Explicit `--numa-bind` or binding lists retain `--membind`. CPU/PCT selection and EngineCore's affinity superset are unchanged.
- If the selected memory policy is rejected or unsupported, retry CPU-only, then unbound. Automatic mode never falls back to strict memory binding.
- Explicit NUMA CLI flags, including binding-list shortcuts, select `spawn` even when `fork` was requested. Omitted flags and `--no-numa-bind` leave start-method selection unchanged.

## Validation

Local validation on macOS, 2026-10-15:

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu VLLM_PLUGINS= PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \
  ../vllm-upstream-kv-metrics/.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  --noconftest -p no:cacheprovider \
  tests/utils_/test_numa_utils.py tests/utils_/test_system_utils.py \
  tests/engine/test_arg_utils.py tests/v1/executor/test_vllm_net_devices.py \
  -q --tb=short
# 258 passed

../vllm-upstream-numa-pcp/.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/config/parallel.py vllm/utils/numa_utils.py vllm/utils/system_utils.py \
  tests/utils_/test_numa_utils.py tests/utils_/test_system_utils.py \
  tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_integration.py \
  docs/configuration/optimization.md
# All applicable hooks passed, including Ruff, mypy and CI test tethering.

git diff --check
# Passed
```

Policy regressions failed against the previous strict implementation before the fix. Unit coverage includes soft worker/EngineCore policy selection, child config reuse, config-copy/hash stability, PCT CPU selection, unsupported preference fallback, inherited memory policies, eligibility/topology checks, and existing PCP/DP indexing regressions. These tests mock host discovery, syscalls, and numactl; `--noconftest` bypasses missing `tblib`, so this is not a full-suite or hardware-serving pass.

The shortcut/start-method reproducer failed in 14 cases before the fix; all 20 cases now pass. It checks unset and explicit `fork` environments, separated/`=value` arguments and supported underscore spellings, plus omitted flags and `--no-numa-bind`. A separate parser → `ParallelConfig` → `get_mp_context()` reproducer confirms explicit lists resolve to enabled binding with `spawn`, while omitted/disabled binding retains `fork`.

Added one non-optional NVIDIA smoke test to the existing `v1-kv-offload` Buildkite suite: `test_simple_cpu_offload_with_auto_numa`. It checks the worker's actual CPU affinity and `numactl --show` policy, offloads KV, resets only the GPU prefix cache, then requires a completed CPU-to-GPU reload counter increase and matching generated tokens. It skips ineligible hosts; a skip is not successful NUMA validation. Existing NVIDIA/AMD `utils_` CI retains unit coverage; no AMD hardware-serving validation is claimed.

Linux/NVIDIA validation on 2026-10-14: **1 passed in 48.82s, zero skips**.

- Hardware/software: one NVIDIA H200, dual-socket Xeon Platinum 8562Y+, 128 logical CPUs and two NUMA nodes; Python 3.12.3, Torch 2.14.0+cu132 / CUDA 13.2, driver 580.173.02.
- Configuration: ungated `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, BF16, TP=1, `mp`/`spawn`, MRV2, eager execution; 128 MiB GPU KV cache and 256 MiB CPU offload pool.
- Observed: EngineCore and worker launched with `--preferred=0`; worker policy was `preferred`, with CPU affinity `0-31,64-95`. After resetting only the GPU prefix cache, **16 blocks completed CPU-to-GPU reload**, and generated token IDs matched the cold run.

The run used the Python implementation at `34a1511ecc` plus the test refinements now committed as `2c535797ed`, with precompiled native artifacts from main `775fefa804ca`. The container image was `vllm/vllm-openai@sha256:a7deff2c216def98c193352aca50fb03a2ee29231355b3033dc3789009f6d23e`. An isolated pytest wrapper used `--noconftest`, supplied the existing test-only `enable_pickle` fixture, and required one executed pass; the Kubernetes Job exited successfully. Full logs are retained locally, without publishing private cluster identifiers.

The test deliberately uses the completed-load counter: the `stored` save-outcome metric classifies hybrid-model boundary handoffs, not Qwen's ordinary full-attention stores. A successful CPU reload proves the earlier offload was usable.

Additional H200 validation on 2026-10-15: **both binding-list startup cases passed**. A GPU-engine reproducer parsed `--numa-bind-nodes 0` and `--numa-bind-cpus=0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7`, each in a fresh process with `fork` pre-set and CUDA uninitialized. Both switched to `spawn` for the NUMA requirement; worker policy was `bind`, with affinity `0-31,64-95` and `0-7` respectively. Each generated the same eight token IDs with Qwen3-0.6B/BF16, TP=1, `mp`, MRV2/eager and a 128 MiB GPU KV cache. The run used `2c535797ed` plus the exact fix committed in `40a39f5c40`, with the same pinned image/native-artifact base described above. The Job completed and exited zero; temporary cluster resources were removed.

**Remaining before this draft is ready:** human line-by-line review. Standard repository/CI reproduction (using the existing root fixtures):

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v -s \
  tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_integration.py::test_simple_cpu_offload_with_auto_numa
```

Constrained-affinity/denied-policy fallback and host-local DP indexing are covered by unit tests; no separate container-permission or multi-node validation campaign is proposed. The smoke test checks normal offload compatibility, not exhaustive host-memory-capacity safety. AMD hardware serving, broad model-quality evaluation, performance measurements, and green remote CI remain unverified. No measured speedup is claimed.

## Details

| Control | Memory policy |
|---|---|
| Omitted (`numa_bind=None`) | Best-effort soft preference; failed eligibility checks or an existing non-default memory policy mean no vLLM-added binding. |
| `--numa-bind` | Strict `--membind`; missing numactl or undetectable topology remains an error. Existing policy-probe fallback applies. |
| `--no-numa-bind` | No vLLM-added binding. |
| `--numa-bind-nodes` / `--numa-bind-cpus` | Imply explicit enablement and retain strict memory policy. Combining with `--no-numa-bind` is rejected. |

Binding lists previously enabled the config without triggering the start-method check, leaving binding ineffective when `fork` was requested. The check now recognizes all three explicit CLI flags, normalizing only the option name so `=value` and underscore spellings work too. Python API start-method requirements remain unchanged.

An internal config flag preserves automatic-policy identity after `numa_bind` resolves to `True`, so spawned workers do not mistake it for explicit strict binding. This launch-local state is excluded from the DP configuration hash; no public flag or steady-state inference operation is added.

Automatic eligibility requires CUDA/ROCm, multiple NUMA nodes, numactl and usable memory-policy support, known unrestricted CPU affinity, a default memory policy, and `spawn` with an `mp`/`uni` executor and `mp` DP. Ray, external/custom launchers, device-ID remapping, fork, and PCP remain excluded. Start-method defaults are unchanged. Each launcher uses host-local NUMA IDs, not cluster-wide IDs.

Soft preference permits allocation on other allowed NUMA nodes when local memory is unavailable, avoiding a new hard node-capacity restriction by default. Explicit strict binding still requires sufficient memory on the selected nodes. The loader's existing RAM estimates and container memory limits are unchanged; policy probes check acceptance, not allocation capacity.

Duplicate-work searches refreshed on 2026-10-15 found no competing upstream GPU automatic-default PR. Other open NUMA work addresses affinity, memory sizing, CPU execution, or ROCm packaging; this PR continues the credited fork trial.
